topic: Business automation for repetitive weekly work

topic: SEO is ongoing, not a launch task
hook: SEO is not something you switch on at launch.

post.headline: SEO is not a launch task
post.myth: SEO is something you set up once when the website goes live.
post.fact: Rankings follow ongoing work: technical fixes, useful content and earned links.

caption:
SEO is not something you switch on at launch.

Search engines reward sites that keep improving: pages that load properly, content that answers real questions, and other sites linking to you.

Pick one page this month and make it the most useful answer to a question your customers ask.

topic: Why a slow site loses enquiries
hook: A slow page loses people before they read a word.

post.headline: Test your site on mobile data, not office Wi-Fi

Open your site that way today. If you are waiting, so are they.

topic: Keep your Google Business Profile current
hook: For many local customers, your Google listing is the first thing they see.

post.subtext: Hours, photos and services that are out of date cost you calls you never hear about.
post.headline: Your Google listing is often your first impression

caption:
For many local customers, your Google listing is the first thing they see.

Before they visit your website, they see your hours, your photos and what other people say about you.

This week, check three things: opening hours, at least a few recent photos, and that every service you offer is listed.

Save this as a quick monthly check.

topic: One page, one call to action
hook: Five buttons on one page usually means zero clicks.

post.subtext: When everything is a button, nothing gets clicked.
post.headline: Every page should ask for one thing.

caption:
Five buttons on one page usually means zero clicks.

Visitors hesitate when a page asks them to call, email, download, subscribe and follow all at once.

Decide the single next step you want from each page, make it obvious, and move everything else lower down.

Want a quick look at your key pages? DM us.

story.text: Pick one next step per page. Make it the biggest button.

topic: What app store optimisation actually covers
hook: A good app can still go unnoticed in the store.

post.subtext: Store listings, creative sets and keyword coverage, tuned and tested.
post.headline: Help the right people find your app

caption:
A good app can still go unnoticed in the store.

App store optimisation is the work of making your listing match what people actually search for, and making the screenshots and description convince them to install.

Start by reading your own listing as a stranger would. Is it clear what the app does in the first line?
